system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

The Seller’s “[STANDARD]”, “FINAL” and alleged principal-level agreement labels do **not** establish Buyer acceptance. Review all positions against the AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free acquisition. The proposals below are Buyer negotiating positions, not assertions of market practice. The underlying SPA and DD documents have not been supplied for verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **AUD 4.8m (20%)**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate protection for fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Reopen; seek 100% of price initially**, with any lower negotiated cap dependent on diligence and meaningful carve-outs — 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket recovering the full qualifying amount once crossed, aggregation of related claims and appropriate category exclusions. | **Counter with AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, excluding fundamental/title, tax and specific indemnity claims — the proposed double filter could materially erode recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties; separate periods for other categories; timely notification preserves claims. | **Seek 36 months, with 24 months as a negotiated fallback**, and reject automatic cross-application — latent issues may not emerge within 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general cap and time limit. | Separate fundamental warranties, including ownership, capacity, valid issue and absence of encumbrances; no basket/de minimis; liability up to at least the price and a substantially longer claim period. | **Reject the general regime; seek a 100% price cap and six-year contractual notification period**, subject to execution and statutory limitation advice — ownership risk should not expire or exhaust alongside ordinary business warranties. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses cover **all Claims of any nature**, without an express fraud exception. | An overriding fraud/fraudulent concealment carve-out covering relevant Seller conduct and attribution, preserving all available remedies. | **Require an express carve-out across every cap, threshold, time bar, disclosure, knowledge and remedies provision** — broad boilerplate must not become an attempted defence to fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; precise warranty cross-references and a frozen, accessible disclosure archive. | **Reject indiscriminate deemed disclosure; require specific disclosures and narrowly defined permitted general disclosures** — document availability is not the same as clear disclosure of a warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Claims barred by Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters discoverable from data-room or public-record searches. | No knowledge exclusion; if unavoidable, only actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without constructive or imputed adviser knowledge. | **Delete; narrowly constrain any fallback and exclude it from specific indemnities** — the Seller should not transfer undiscovered risks through a deemed duty to investigate. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence satisfying associated conditions supplied. | A Buyer-benefit completion condition requiring valid, effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable commercial changes. | **Make satisfactory consent and associated conditions a completion gate**, waivable only by Buyer, with a long-stop termination right — approximately 30% of FY26 revenue depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release provided after Completion. | Repayment through controlled completion funds flow, binding payout arrangements and effective security releases at Completion, with prompt registry updates. | **Reject an unsecured post-Completion release promise; require a coordinated payout/release mechanism and debt deduction without double counting** — Buyer must receive a debt-free, unencumbered business. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; Seller calls them its matter; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears sale-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with clear payment responsibility and employee conditions. | **Itemise and fund the full liability through the completion adjustment/funds flow, backed by an indemnity for unpaid amounts** — otherwise a Seller transaction expense may remain in the acquired company. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; records show **AUD 180,000 open**, but non-payment is not independently verified and no assignment evidence is supplied. | Verified payment status and an effective assignment/confirmation of all relevant IP rights; protection for ownership defects, third-party claims and remediation costs. | **Require payment and IP-title cure before Completion, plus a broader standalone indemnity outside general thresholds and cap** — paying a fee alone may not resolve the ownership defect or its consequences. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, expected immaterial; unintended recipient received a link potentially covering approximately **1,240 records**; access and notification requirements unresolved. | Prompt scoped investigation, access/log evidence, containment, legally assessed notification obligations and protection against pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require investigation and agreed remediation before Completion, plus a specific indemnity for resulting losses and lawful response costs** — unresolved access and notification facts prevent a reliable materiality conclusion, but do not establish a confirmed breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Combined assessment of timing, scope, enforceability, termination rights, accrual and commercial necessity; controls on new or renewed commitments. | **Review the three together and require Buyer consent if outside agreed ordinary-course limits; adjust price only where their proper classification warrants it** — related commitments should not escape scrutiny through splitting, but are not automatically debt-like. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply across all Claims; administrative simplicity supports common treatment. | Express, coordinated regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title warranties, tax, specific indemnities, price/debt adjustments, covenants and fraud. | **Insert a claim-category matrix and overriding carve-outs with clear priority rules** — protections are ineffective if catch-all definitions silently pull them back into general limitations. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller as holder of 100%; relied on as title evidence. | Independent reconciliation of the register, ASIC records, issue/transfer history, constitution, certificates and relevant encumbrances/options; valid transfer and registration deliverables. | **Verify the complete capitalisation and title chain, supported by fundamental warranties and completion documents** — a register entry alone does not establish an unencumbered, fully transferable 100% interest. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity with an appropriately extended period and tailored exclusions/conduct rules; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties with suitable survival and cap. | **Reopen both: seek tax protection through applicable assessment/recovery periods plus a buffer, and a separately negotiated IP regime alongside the Ironquay indemnity** — tax exposure and core SaaS IP risk are not adequately addressed by an 18-month, 20% general regime. |

**Drafting priority:** ensure disclosure and Buyer knowledge do not qualify specific indemnities or completion conditions, and prohibit double recovery without inadvertently excluding legitimate alternative claims.
=== END ADVICE ===
